questions.question: Picture a Cartesian plane described in words: the x-axis runs across the bottom with whole numbers 0 to 8 marked evenly, and the y-axis runs up the left side with whole numbers 0 to 8 marked evenly. Starting at the origin (0, 0), point A is 3 units to the right and 5 units up. Which ordered pair names point A?
questions.explain: In an ordered pair the first number is always the x-coordinate (how far right) and the second is the y-coordinate (how far up), so 3 right and 5 up is (3, 5). The usual trap is writing (5, 3) by putting the up-number first.

questions.question: On a coordinate grid the x-axis is numbered 0 to 10 across the bottom and the y-axis is numbered 0 to 10 up the left side, one unit per gridline. A friend gives you the ordered pair (6, 2). Which set of steps plots it correctly?
options: Start at the origin, move 2 units right, then 6 units up
Start at the origin, move 6 units right, then 2 units up
Start at the origin, move 6 units right, then 6 units up
Start at the origin, move 8 units right along the x-axis
questions.explain: Read the pair in order: the 6 is the x-coordinate, so travel 6 right along the x-axis first, then the 2 is the y-coordinate, so climb 2 up. Moving 2 right and 6 up swaps the numbers and lands you on a completely different point.

questions.question: Imagine a Cartesian plane with whole numbers 0 to 12 marked on both axes. Point B sits right on the x-axis, exactly 7 units to the right of the origin, and it never leaves that bottom line. Which ordered pair names point B?
questions.explain: A point sitting on the x-axis has climbed 0 units up, so its y-coordinate is 0, giving (7, 0). Writing (0, 7) swaps the numbers and describes a point 7 units up the y-axis instead.

questions.question: On a grid whose x-axis is numbered 0 to 10 across the bottom and whose y-axis is numbered 0 to 10 up the left side, point K is placed exactly where the vertical gridline through 9 crosses the horizontal gridline through 4. What is the ordered pair for point K?
questions.explain: The vertical gridline tells you the x-coordinate (9) and the horizontal gridline tells you the y-coordinate (4), so the point is (9, 4). Many students read the horizontal line first and write (4, 9), which is a different spot on the grid.

questions.question: At a Richmond night market, the map is a Cartesian plane with whole-number gridlines. The bubble-tea stall is at (2, 5). The dumpling stall is 3 units right of the bubble-tea stall and 2 units above it. What ordered pair names the dumpling stall?
questions.explain: Add the slide to each coordinate in order: 2 + 3 = 5 for x and 5 + 2 = 7 for y, so the stall is at (5, 7). The common trap is writing (7, 5), which swaps the across-number and the up-number.

questions.question: On a Cartesian plane, point A is at (2, 4) and point B is at (9, 4). Which statement about these two points is true?
options: They are 7 units apart with one directly above the other
They are 7 units apart and sit side by side on the same horizontal line
They are 5 units apart on the same horizontal line
They are 13 units apart
questions.explain: Both points have the same y-coordinate of 4, so they are at the same height and the gap is only across: 9 − 2 = 7 units. Students who think the first number means ‘up' decide one point is above the other, but it is the second number that controls height.

questions.question: On the same Cartesian plane, point A is at (3, 8) and point B is at (8, 3). Which statement is true?
options: Point A is farther right than point B
A and B are the same point because they use the same two numbers
Point A is higher up the plane than point B
Both points sit on the x-axis
questions.explain: Compare the y-coordinates for height: A has y = 8 and B has y = 3, so A is higher; compare the x-coordinates for across: A has x = 3 and B has x = 8, so B is farther right. Same digits in a different order make a different point, because order is what an ordered pair is all about.

questions.question: A counter on a game board is at (7, 2) on a first-quadrant grid. Which ordered pair names the square that is exactly 4 units directly above it?
questions.explain: Moving straight up changes only the y-coordinate, so x stays 7 and y becomes 2 + 4 = 6, giving (7, 6). Watch out for (6, 7), which swaps the two numbers and sends the counter sideways instead.

questions.question: Maya is asked to plot (3, 5) on a first-quadrant grid. She starts at the origin, moves 3 units UP first, then 5 units RIGHT, and marks her point there. Which choice correctly describes where Maya's mark actually landed and why?
options: Her mark is at (5, 3); she used the x-number to go up and the y-number to go right
Her mark is at (3, 5); with ordered pairs the order of the two numbers does not matter
Her mark is at (3, 3); she counted the same number twice
Her mark is at (8, 8); she added the two numbers together
questions.explain: Maya ended up 5 right and 3 up, which is the point (5, 3), not (3, 5). The first number in an ordered pair is always the across (x) move and the second is always the up (y) move, so swapping them gives a genuinely different point.

questions.question: A map of a Burnaby skate park is drawn on a Cartesian plane with whole-number gridlines. The water fountain is at (4, 3). The bench is 5 units right of the fountain. The bike rack is 2 units above the bench. What ordered pair names the bike rack?
questions.explain: Do the steps one at a time: the bench is (4 + 5, 3) = (9, 3), then the bike rack is 2 higher, so (9, 3 + 2) = (9, 5). Two traps here are stopping at the bench and writing the pair backwards as (5, 9).

questions.question: On a class map of a park drawn on a Cartesian plane, the totem pole is marked at (6, 0). Sam says that means it is 6 units right of the origin, sitting on the x-axis. Priya says it means it is 6 units up from the origin, sitting on the y-axis. Who is right?
options: Priya is right; the first number tells you how far up to go, since you count up before you count across
Both are right; (6, 0) and (0, 6) land on the same spot, because they use the same two numbers
Sam is right; the first number is the x-coordinate, counted right from the origin along the x-axis
Neither is right; (6, 0) means 6 units right and 6 units up, because the 6 counts for both directions
questions.explain: The first number of an ordered pair is the x-coordinate, so (6, 0) is 6 units right and 0 units up, right on the x-axis. The pair (0, 6) is Priya's point, and it lands somewhere completely different, which shows why order matters.

questions.question: In a board game on a first-quadrant Cartesian plane, a piece starts at (2, 6). It slides 4 units right, then slides 3 units down. What ordered pair names its finishing square?
questions.explain: Sliding right adds to x (2 + 4 = 6) and sliding down subtracts from y (6 − 3 = 3), so the piece finishes at (6, 3). Writing (3, 6) swaps the across-number and the up-number, and moving up instead of down gives the wrong height.
